messages:
Elaine: Quick question — customer (AcmeCloud) wants a Dedicated POC but their app runs on ephemeral worker nodes behind a corporate proxy. They can only allowlist static egress IPs. Two asks: (1) can we provide static egress IPs for Dedicated? (2) ballpark pricing for a 1–2 GPU POC (2 weeks). Also they need a scoped API key for the POC. Any blockers?

Sam: Short answer: yes, a few paths. Options: (a) customer-managed NAT with a static IP (they allowlist our endpoint host/ip), (b) Redwood-managed static egress add-on for Dedicated (we reserve a small set of NAT IPs), (c) Private deployment or VPC peering if they need full network isolation. Which option does the customer prefer?

Elaine: They prefer not to touch infra — ideally we provide static egress IPs or proxy through our side so they only allowlist a couple IPs.

Kai: If they can't change infra, Redwood-managed static egress is simplest. For Dedicated endpoints traffic egresses from our egress NAT pool, so we can publish 2–4 IPv4 addresses for them to allowlist. If they require TLS client certs or mTLS to a corporate proxy, that gets trickier. Need to confirm whether they're hitting a public Dedicated endpoint (recommended) vs trying to peer into a Private deployment.

Jordan: Security checklist: please have them complete our standard security questionnaire. We'll need SOC2 attestations and to document data handling for the POC. For static egress we provide an architecture diagram, IP ranges, and logs retention info. Also capture a named contact and the exact IP/CIDR they will allowlist on their firewall.

Ben: Ballpark pricing to feed the deal: small Dedicated POC (1–2 GPUs for 2 weeks) — roughly $3k–5k total depending on model and throughput. Redwood-managed static egress add-on — typically $300–700/month (we prorate for short POC). Scoped short-lived API key and trial credits we can issue for the POC. I'll confirm exact numbers with Billing and return a quote.

Elaine: Can someone draft a tiny allowlist table and a sample curl I can send to the customer? Also I'll need the T&Cs for a short POC MSA.

Sam: Draft allowlist + sample below — edit as needed.

```
Allowlist table (send to customer):
- Destination hostname: dedicated-us-1.redwood.ai (TLS)
- Example egress IPv4s (replace with canonical values we provide): 54.23.180.12, 54.23.180.13
- Ports: 443 outbound

Firewall rule example (ACL):
- Allow outbound to 54.23.180.12/32 port 443

Sample curl (POC key placeholder):
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer POC_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' \
  https://dedicated-us-1.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Kai: Note — IPs above are illustrative. I'll provision the dedicated egress pool for the POC and post the canonical /32s in the ENG ticket. Also calling out: if they require IPv6 or enterprise NAT64 we need to discuss further.

Jordan: I'm attaching the questionnaire link for them to complete: <https://redwood.sharepoint/security/questionnaire.pdf>. Also request their data retention expectations and whether logs should be redacted for the POC.

deploy-bot: Created ticket ENG-2021 for egress IP provisioning, scoped POC pool, and security handoff. <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-2021>

Elaine: Thanks everyone — I'll send this to the customer now, ask them to return the allowlist and sign the short POC MSA. Jordan/Ben/Kai please comment on the ticket with final numbers and the canonical IPs. :thumbsup:
